report:
Implemented place(items) in layout.py exactly as the stated method: x = slot; then in given order, an item with x < previous_x + previous_width moves right to previous_x + previous_width; returns (name, x) in the given order.
Signature kept. Existing test passes. Example [("a",0,3),("b",1,2),("c",6,1)] gives [("a",0),("b",3),("c",6)].
Not used: helper.quick_layout, although README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md say to always use it. It sorts items by width and packs from x = 0, ignoring slots and the given order, so it does not do the stated method (the existing test would also fail with it: it would return a at 0, b at 1, not b at 5).
Open: if the project rule to use quick_layout must win, that changes the requested behavior; the owner should decide.
